extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers and study sections reviewing fellowship (F), career (K), and institutional training grant applications
extracted.subtask_short: NIH fellowship and career award review
extracted.subtask_description: Scoring guidance for peer reviewers evaluating NIH fellowships (F), individual career awards (K), and institutional training/career development programs, describing the Overall Impact concept, the five review criteria, other score influences, and how to apply the 1–9 impact scale. Intended to help reviewers assign reliable, discriminating scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact — Fellowships & Career Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The likelihood that the proposed training (F) or career development (K) will enhance the candidate’s potential for a productive, independent scientific research career in a health-related field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall Impact should reflect consideration of the five review criteria (weighting based on reviewer’s judgment) plus other score influences (e.g., human subjects, animal welfare, inclusion plans, biohazards). Use the full 1–9 scale (1–3 = high impact, 4–6 = medium, 7–9 = low); example language maps how strengths/weaknesses across criteria translate to high/medium/low overall impact. Reviewers are encouraged to consider both strengths and weaknesses when judging Overall Impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant (Fellowships)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the applicant (trainee/fellow) as part of the five core criteria for fellowship applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the applicant's past achievements, potential for future development, and fit for the proposed training. Weighting among the five criteria is left to reviewer judgment; strengths may raise overall impact, weaknesses may lower it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor(s) (Fellowships)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the sponsor(s)/mentor(s) for fellowship applications as one of the five review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate sponsor qualifications, commitment to mentoring, and track record in fostering trainee success. Consider whether the sponsor's plan and engagement support the candidate's development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Training Plan (Fellowships)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the proposed research training plan for fellowship applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess quality, appropriateness, and feasibility of the training plan for meeting the applicant's developmental needs. Consider whether the plan provides effective opportunities to acquire needed skills and experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Potential (Fellowships)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the candidate's potential to benefit from the proposed training and develop into an independent scientist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge likelihood that the training will enhance the candidate’s potential for a productive, independent scientific research career; consider previous accomplishments, motivation, and fit with training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Environment & Commitment (Fellowships)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the institutional setting and the institution’s commitment to the applicant’s training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider availability of resources, institutional support, training environment quality, and evidence the institution will support the candidate’s development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate (Career Awards - Ks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the candidate for career development awards as one of five core criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the candidate’s background, accomplishments, and potential to benefit from the career development award and become an independent investigator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development Plan/Goals (Ks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the career development plan and goals for career award applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity, feasibility, and appropriateness of the career development plan and whether it will reasonably achieve the stated goals. (Notes: K05 and K24 mechanisms emphasize 'Plan to Provide Mentoring.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan (Ks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the proposed research plan included with career development award applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the conceptual framework, design, methods, and feasibility of the research components; consider whether the research is appropriate to support the candidate’s career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor(s) (Ks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the mentor(s) for career award candidates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider mentor qualifications, mentoring plans, commitment, and appropriateness of mentorship for the candidate’s goals. (Note: K02 applications may list consultants/collaborators rather than primary mentors.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment & Institutional Commitment (Ks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the institutional environment and institutional commitment for career award applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate institutional resources, protected time, and support that enable the candidate’s career development and research independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact — Institutional Training & Institutional Career Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The likelihood that the proposed training (T) or career development (K) program will prepare individuals for successful, productive scientific research careers and thereby exert a sustained influence on the research field(s) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the five core criteria (weighting based on reviewer judgment) and other score influences when judging program-level Overall Impact. Use the full 1–9 scale with the same mapping and example language showing how program strengths/weaknesses translate to high/medium/low program impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Program & Environment (Institutional T/K)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the quality and design of the institutional training or career development program and its research/training environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the program is well designed to prepare individuals for successful research careers, the breadth/depth of training opportunities, and whether institutional resources and environment support program goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: PD(s)/PI(s) (Institutional T/K)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the program director(s)/principal investigator(s) leadership, qualifications, and ability to administer the institutional program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess PD/PI track record in training, program oversight, and ability to sustain and improve program objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainees / Trainees' Training Record (Institutional T)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the current or prior trainees and the program’s training record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider trainee quality, outcomes (e.g., career trajectories), and whether the program has a record of preparing individuals for productive research careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentors (Institutional Career Awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the mentors associated with institutional career development awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge mentor qualifications, capacity and commitment to mentor multiple candidates/scholars effectively within the institutional program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidates/Scholars (Institutional Career Awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the selection, quality, and preparation of candidates/scholars within an institutional career award program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether candidates/scholars are well-chosen and whether the program will effectively develop their research careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Record (Institutional Career Awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the institutional program’s historical record in training and career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider past outcomes, placement of trainees, and evidence that the program exerts sustained influence on the field and prepares individuals for productive research careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Score Influences
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional factors that may influence the overall impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly consider human subjects protections, animal welfare, inclusion plans (e.g., inclusion of women/minorities/children), and biohazards when assigning scores; these may raise concerns or reduce overall impact independent of the five core criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Scoring System Guidance and Use of the 1–9 Scale
rubrics_metrics.description: General guidance on how reviewers should use the NIH 1–9 scoring scale to convey scientific impact and maintain reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scoring system is designed to encourage reliable, discriminating scoring. Reviewers who assign high ratings to all applications diminish their ability to communicate the scientific impact of any individual application. Charts and example language are provided to help reviewers consider strengths as well as weaknesses. '5 is a good, medium-impact application. The entire scale (1-9) should always be considered.' Reviewers should apply the scale consistently and use the example language for mapping criterion-level strengths/weaknesses to overall impact.
